text: The authors note the protocol is safe to use without confidence in stability, but a prover that only knows unstable decompositions into solvable subproblems cannot get some problems judged accurately even when both debaters know the answer. They pose whether stability is necessary, suggest problems might split into those needing precise dependence on subclaims (e.g. mathematical proofs, perhaps checked as Lean proofs) and those that do not (e.g. noisy empirical evidence), and say progress requires characterising which problems admit stable decompositions.
title: Open: is stability necessary, and which problems admit stable decompositions?
